comments.content: The `disable` method passes `!${scopePath}` to `enable`, but `Override.fromInput` expects a path without the '!' prefix (it checks `inputRule.startsWith('!')` to determine `isDisable`). This will cause the path to be incorrectly parsed with a leading '!' character in `baseRule`.

The `disable` method calls `enable` with `includeSubdirs` parameter, but disable operations should likely have their own `includeSubdirs` logic. Currently, disabling a workspace would use the same `includeSubdirs` value as enabling, which may not be the intended behavior.
The success message uses `args.scope` directly, but when `args.scope` is undefined (defaulting to User scope), this will print 'undefined' in the message. Should use the resolved scope value instead.
Same issue: success message uses `args.scope` directly which will be 'undefined' when not provided. Should display the resolved scope (User) instead.
